name: skill-revocation-sweep
description: Use when a skill is being retired, deleted, revoked or replaced, above all one withdrawn because it was unsafe or wrong. Removing the registry entry does not revoke a skill, because an agent can rebuild it from residual carriers such as installed copies, published packages, archives, transcripts and memory entries. List every surface that carries the skill, clear them in one pass with the source first, leave a tombstone that says the skill was withdrawn and why, and test revocation by whether the behaviour can still be rebuilt, not by whether the directory is gone. Distinct from skill-causal-curation (decides keep, repair or retire) and done-retirement (work items, not skills). Backed by the OBLIVION skill-unlearning benchmark (arxiv 2608.08264). Triggers on retiring, deleting or revoking a skill.
